title: Pharaoh's broken arms
english: The arms of Pharaoh are wickedness in sinful action, and the mind of the flesh in impious teachings. God breaks these arms because He is good. Pharaoh is a symbol of the devil, the ruler of sin among human beings. The Lord breaks the arm of sinners so that they cannot grasp a sword.
orientation: Origen is beginning his commentary on Ezekiel 30:25, explaining the symbolic meaning of Pharaoh's arms.

title: Allegory of Pharaoh's watering and the Hebrew word for pit and length
english: This above all shows the allegory of Scripture: Pharaoh would not literally water the earth from his excrements, but the filthy discharge of the adversary waters earthly things.

The Hebrew has “in the length of the pit.” For the word iarech, pronounced with aspiration in the Hebrew tongue, means both “thigh” and “length.” The pit, therefore, he calls the depth of burial, and length the extent of burial.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Ezekiel 32, explaining that Pharaoh's watering of the land must be read allegorically, and then discussing the Hebrew word behind 'pit' in Ezekiel 32:23.

title: The closed east gate as the hidden mysteries of God
english: Ezekiel, the son of man, describes many gates, and he has something to say about each one. Now he speaks to those who have ears about the gate of the holy things that faces east. It is written of it: “This gate shall be closed,” and so on (Ezekiel 44:1). It is closed not only because the Lord, the God of Israel, passes through the gate, but also because the prince sits in that gate to eat before the Lord by way of Ailam, which means the vestibule of the gate (Ezekiel 44:3).

The closed gate is the mysteries of God, the unclosed things. Knowledge has a key, as the Lord says to the lawyers (Luke 11:52). So the gate is closed to human beings, for what is inside the gate is what no eye has seen and no ear has heard, and so on (1 Corinthians 2:9).

The sealed scroll written about in Isaiah has the same meaning as this gate (Isaiah 29:11). You will find this same scroll more clearly in the Revelation of John, along with what is written about it, and how the one from the tribe of Judah opened these things, and he alone (Revelation 5:5). For until our Lord Jesus Christ came, the law and the prophetic word were closed, and over them lay a veil, the stone of hardness, which Jacob removed from the well. In many places Scripture has opened up the meaning of this gate.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Ezekiel's vision of the closed east gate of the sanctuary, interpreting it as the hidden mysteries of God.
